findings.title: Ledger strict mode is a cached client check that fails open (Cypher writes)
findings.intended: In strict mode a guarded Cypher write raises LedgerStrictModeError and changes nothing (specs/213-graph-revision-ledger/contracts/ledger-api.md:82-92; CYP-X7.2). Decision HD-0801 (assumption): keep modelling the Python guard, cache and fail-open; the intended refusal still applies.
findings.observed: Live, two IRIS processes on AUDITB (b-08-live-f0801): process A's engine wrote once (guard cached state never-enabled); process B enabled the ledger and set strict (Meta: enabled, strict, head_seq 1); 0.28 s later A ran `CREATE (:B08G {id:'b08_g1'})`, which succeeded (row written, journal: nodes/rdf_labels/rdf_props/^KG) and was not recorded (head_seq 1 before and after). B's fresh engine was refused at once and A was refused after the 5 s TTL (LedgerStrictModeError). Source: guard caches Meta for TTL_SECONDS=5.0 and treats any probe exception as never-enabled (iris_vector_graph/ledger/guard.py:20, 38-59); the Cypher path checks it only on the transactional SQL route (query.py:2299-2301). Unit tests pinning the window and fail-open pass (b-08-run-unit).
findings.remedy: Either document the 5 s window and fail-open in ledger-api.md and USER_GUIDE, or check strict mode fail-closed per write (or server-side in Txn_Begin / a trigger) so raw SQL and other clients are covered (HD-0801 options b/c).
findings.notes: Module 11 owns the guard machine (b-mc-m11-guard-as-built-ttl, -as-built-failopen, -reviewed, -control-failopen). Fail-open on a failing probe is shown by the passing unit test only (a live probe failure needs a privilege change, not allowed here). Side effect of this check: the AUDITB ledger went never-enabled -> enabled (genesis seq 1) -> disabled, strict off; a never-enabled state cannot be restored without PurgeAll. Rerun under the iris lock after the 23:02:53-23:03:40 UTC incident window matched the original (b-08-live-f0801-rerun, b-08-run-unit-rerun).

new_findings.title: A rolled-back Cypher edge write leaves the interned snapshot's counters raised
new_findings.intended: SYS-I8 (CONTEXT.md:109-120): a store built from others matches them or says it is out of date; CYP-I6.4: a failed write query takes back all of its steps.
new_findings.observed: Live: with ^NKG built (engine.sync()), a query that creates edge b08_r1-[:B08NEW]->b08_r2 and then fails (duplicate literal edge) rolled back the row and the ^NKG(-1/-2) entries, but ^NKG(-3, idx(b08_r1)) went 1 -> 2 and ^NKG("$meta","edgeCount") 2 -> 3, with no stale mark (Adjacency.Put $Increments them, Adjacency.cls:95-107; $INCREMENT is not undone by TROLLBACK). The journal shows these records outside the transaction (b-08-live-footprints).
gates: 3.3a-writesets (^NKG counters written by every edge writer)
new_findings.remedy: Either keep the counters inside the transaction (SET from the merged degree, as BuildNKG's sweep does) or mark ^NKG stale when a writer's transaction rolls back; or document ^NKG(-3) and edgeCount as upper bounds (admin.py already treats edgeCount as an over-count).
new_findings.notes: Owning code is module 04 (Adjacency.cls) / module 10 (^NKG readers); found through module 08's rollback. No reader at the pin uses the ^NKG(-3) value except the rebuild (readers iterate it: NKGAccelAdjacency.cls:19, NKGAccelCentrality.cls:473); admin.py:808-816 knowingly tolerates edgeCount over-counts, so whether these counters are contract-bearing is undecided. The ^KG("gen") over-bump is documented as harmless (Adjacency.cls:23-30). Rerun under the iris lock after the 23:02:53-23:03:40 UTC incident window matched the original (b-08-live-fc0801-rollback-nkg-rerun, b-08-live-footprints-rerun).

new_findings.title: MERGE ... ON CREATE SET r = a gives every merged relationship the first row's properties
new_findings.intended: openCypher: MERGE runs once per incoming row; `SET r = a` copies that row's node a onto that row's relationship (CYP-B6.8 per-row MERGE semantics); gate §3.4 storage-order.
new_findings.observed: Live (b-08-live-storage-order): `MATCH (a:B08PP), (t:B08TT {id:'b08_tt'}) MERGE (a)-[r:B08MR3]->(t) ON CREATE SET r = a` with a = b08_p1 {city:'ca', pop:1} and b08_p2 {city:'cb', pop:2} created two relationships whose qualifiers were both {id:'b08_p1', city:'ca', pop:'1'}. The translator copies `(SELECT TOP 1 a.node_id FROM <preceding rows>)` (translator.py:12362-12395) with no ORDER BY and applies one UPDATE to every merged relationship, so the stored values come from whichever row storage order puts first.
new_findings.remedy: Correlate the copied node with each relationship's own row (per-row UPDATE through the row-bound MERGE plan, or a correlated subquery on the relationship's source/target), or refuse `SET r = a` when the preceding clauses bind more than one row; live test with two rows.
